generatedFor: The End of the F***ing World

beats.label: S1 · Plan to kill her
beats.text: James, sure he is a psychopath, picks new schoolmate Alyssa as his next kill; when she begs him to run away, he agrees, planning to murder her later.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the false premise the whole season is quietly dismantling.

beats.label: S1 · Road turns dangerous
beats.text: The stolen Mercedes crashes and their money runs out; a predatory driver, Martin, gropes James in a bathroom, and Alyssa quietly blackmails him for his wallet.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First time Alyssa protects James — the dynamic starts inverting.

beats.label: S1 · He can't do it
beats.text: They squat in author Clive Koch's empty house; watching Alyssa sleep, James finds he cannot bring the knife down and realises he is in love with her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The private turning point of James's arc — the psychopath story ends here.

beats.label: S1 · The killing
beats.text: Koch comes home and tries to rape Alyssa; James stabs him dead. They flee the scene, leaving behind the knife, Topher's wallet, and Koch's tapes of past victims.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The crime the police chase for the rest of the season, and the evidence trail they follow.

beats.label: S1 · The detectives close in
beats.text: DCs Noon and Darego pick up the trail; Koch's mother hands over her son's tapes of past victims, opening a self-defence angle that could reduce the charge to manslaughter.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the legal question of what actually awaits them if caught, and the split between the two detectives.

beats.label: S1 · Father betrays her
beats.text: Alyssa finds her long-absent father Leslie, a drug dealer with a secret second son; recognising the pair from a TV reward notice, he secretly calls 999 pretending to help.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes Alyssa's search for her father as a wound rather than a homecoming, and triggers the beach endgame.

beats.label: S1 · Beach and a gunshot
beats.text: Cornered on the beach, Alyssa knocks Noon out and grabs the shotgun; James takes it off her, knocks her down to pin everything on himself, and runs — a single shot cracks.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The unresolved image the next season opens on: Alyssa on the sand, James's fate a gunshot.

cliffhanger.text: James sprints across the beach with Leslie's shotgun, drawing armed police away from Alyssa so she cannot be charged. A single gunshot fires as the screen cuts to black; whether he is alive is left unsaid.
questions: With James gone, will Alyssa still face charges over Koch's death?
Can DC Noon's self-defence argument survive her partner Darego pushing for manslaughter?

characters.name: James
characters.line: 17, once convinced he was a psychopath; killed Clive Koch to save Alyssa, realised he loved her, and drew armed police onto himself so she could escape.

characters.name: Alyssa
characters.line: 17, restless runaway from a hostile stepfather; the one who dragged James on the road, came to genuinely love him, and knocked out DC Noon to buy him a chance.

characters.name: DC Eunice Noon
characters.line: The sympathetic detective who worked out Koch's killing was self-defence and tried to bring the pair in gently; last seen knocked unconscious on the beach.

characters.name: DC Teri Darego
characters.line: Noon's by-the-book partner, who sees only the crime and not the context, pushing hard for a manslaughter charge regardless.

characters.name: Leslie
characters.line: Alyssa's estranged father, a small-time drug dealer with an abandoned second son; feigned a welcome then dialled 999 the moment he recognised the reward money.

characters.name: Gwen
characters.line: Alyssa's mother, cowed by her husband Tony; only now learning from police that her daughter is a murder suspect on the run.
characters.note: May be who Alyssa turns to if she goes home.

characters.name: Phil
characters.line: James's gentle, oblivious father; devastated by the theft of his Mercedes and the news that his son is wanted.
